rfm_tuples.R: We delivered strong year-over-year 18% revenue growth and shipped a record 2 billion Ceva-powered units... a record 1.1 billion Bluetooth devices, a record 179 million Wi-Fi devices, a record 170 million cellular IoT devices, 340 million smartphones, and 170 million other smart edge devices powered by our DSPs, AI Accelerators and sensor fusion software.

CEVA's royalty revenues = ~44% of total $106.9M = ~$47.0M on 2B units, implying ~$0.024/unit blended ASP. Reasonable for connectivity IP. Royalty as % total rev climbed 38% (2022) -> 41% (2023) -> 44% (2024), consistent with shipped-volume ramp.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Volume series ties out: 1.70B (2022) -> 1.62B (2023, -4%) -> 2.00B (2024, +23%). Royalty % climb (38->41->44) is internally consistent with stronger royalty growth (+18%) vs total (+9.8%). Unit math reasonable for an IP licensor.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Quantitative, multi-year, internally consistent volume disclosure with unit-by-product breakdown. This is the OPPOSITE of an issuer hiding behind 'design-win' adjectives. Honest IP licensor pattern.

rfm_tuples.R: Wi-Fi represents a significant royalty revenue opportunity in connection with our leading market position in licensing Wi-Fi 6 and our leadership position in Wi-Fi 7 IP... leading market position in licensing Wi-Fi 6 with more than 40 customers to date and leadership position in Wi-Fi 7 IP.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: Specificity check on 'leadership' claims. Promotional issuers say 'leading' without numbers; honest issuers name customer counts, design-win counts, and shipment metrics. Are Wi-Fi 6/7 claims backed with concrete metrics?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Concrete metrics provided: >40 Wi-Fi 6 customers; record 66M Wi-Fi units Q4 2024 (179M FY24); explicit Wi-Fi architecture deal with 'one of the world's leading MCU companies' Q4 2024; Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6/7 design-wins disclosed. Bluetooth claimed >30% worldwide market share (excluding mobile) with 1.1B Bluetooth units shipped.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 'Leadership' claims are backstopped with counts (40+, 30%, 1.1B, 179M). This is what honest IP-licensor disclosure looks like. Mode B finding: no 'we expect Wi-Fi 7 to be a huge market' hand-wave — the disclosure pairs each forward claim with a current shipment number.

rfm_tuples.R: Royalty revenues were approximately 44%, 41% and 38% of our total revenues for 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively... Licensing and related revenue was $60.0 million, representing a 4% increase in 2024 as compared to 2023. We signed 43 licensing agreements... down from 53 last year.

summary: CEVA's FY24 10-K is an honest IP-licensor filing with no material distress signals. Despite the GAAP net loss of $8.8M, the underlying business shows operating leverage (loss arc $23.2M -> $11.9M -> $8.8M, all driven by $15.6M SBC), $163.6M cash with ZERO debt, expanding royalty mix (38% -> 44% of revenue), record unit shipments (2B+, including 1.1B Bluetooth and 179M Wi-Fi with quantified market positions), 25-year auditor continuity (Kost Forer/EY Israel), real and growing buyback execution ($8.5M in 2024 + 700K-share authorization added Nov 2024), and transparent customer concentration (Customer A stable in 13-16% band, AR concentration declining). Mode B findings: Item 9B = 'None' (no insider plan activity), licensing deal count drop (53 -> 43) is disclosed without spin, Israel-Hamas war risk named with specifics. The S&P 600 removal post-cutoff reflects GRADUATION (the index committee said 'no longer representative of the small cap market space'), not distress — confirming the +83% forward return. The honesty-alpha framework MUST exclude CEVA from short candidates; treating delisted_or_distressed as automatic short would convert this into an -83% false positive. This is the strongest exclusion-as-alpha validation case in the pilot batch.
